title: "Contribute & Disclaimer"

## Contribute

No dataset is ever perfect or complete.

Therefore, and firstly, please let us know if you spot any errors or problems in the materials we provide — see [Team](equipo.qmd) for contact details.

There are also ways in which CONDLA could still be extended. We are lacking the time and resources to do all of this ourselves, but would be grateful for input from others interested in contributing, and will provide what help and assistance we can.

Examples of opportunities for further development include:

- **Extending the time series.** The dataset currently runs through 2026. As countries reform their CCT programs, the coding could be extended to cover new rules as they are enacted.
- **Implementation, not just design.** CONDLA codes the *design* of conditionality (what the rules say), not how consistently they are enforced in practice. As our own paper on the dataset notes, information on implementation practices is patchy and was not included in this version. Anyone with systematic data on enforcement in a given program is welcome to get in touch.
- **Expert review coverage.** The codebook's country-expert review currently covers 8 of the 16 countries (Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Guatemala, Honduras, Paraguay, and Peru). We would welcome country experts for Brazil, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, or Uruguay willing to review the coding for their country.

## Disclaimer

You can download and use the data, codebook, and script provided here free of charge for research purposes. If you do, please cite the dataset as:

> Antía, Florencia, Cecilia Rossel, Sofía Karsaclian, Sebastián Pineyro, and Melisa Moreno. 2026. *CONDLA: Conditionalities in Latin America Database*.

You may not sell any of the materials obtained here, or incorporate them into another dataset without our explicit permission. Please do not redistribute a modified version of these files as if it were the original.

We have taken care to produce accurate, well-documented data, but cannot guarantee that the dataset and accompanying files are entirely free of errors. If you detect one, or would like to suggest a correction, please contact us (see [Team](equipo.qmd)). We accept no liability for damages arising from the use of the materials provided here.
